source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

04005.t:
In the race for governor, Coconino County backed Hobbs over Biggs by 38 points, 37,136 votes to 16,311, up from Harris's 20-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 18-point move toward the Democrats puts it seventh of Arizona's 15 counties, all of which moved left, and matches the typical county in the state. It outpaced the typical national move of 14 points. Counties with similar 2024 results moved by comparable amounts: Apache by 20 points, Pima by 16 and Santa Cruz by 27.

Turnout fell sharply. The 54,883 votes cast were 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04013.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Maricopa County went from a 4-point Trump win in 2024 to a 16-point win for Hobbs over Biggs, 874,335 votes to 626,744. That is a 20-point move toward the Democrats, a little more than the state's 19 and the typical Arizona county's 18, and well above the typical national move of 14. Every one of Arizona's 15 counties moved left; Maricopa ranked fourth and was one of two that flipped from Trump to the Democrat. Comparable counties moved by similar amounts: Pima 16 points, Pinal 19.

Turnout fell sharply. The 1,526,333 votes cast were 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

04007.t:
Gila County stayed firmly Republican in the race for Arizona governor, but by less than in 2024. Biggs beat Hobbs here 12,786 to 7,620, a margin of 25 points, down from Trump's 38-point win over Harris. That 13-point shift toward the Democrats is smaller than the typical Arizona county's 18 points, ranking 13th of 15 in a state where every county moved left and Hobbs won by 13.

Turnout fell sharply: 20,877 votes were cast, about 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved about as much: Yavapai shifted 12 points and La Paz 13, while tiny Greenlee swung 30.

04012.t:
La Paz County stayed firmly Republican in the race for governor but moved 13 points toward the Democrats. Biggs beat Hobbs here 3,392 to 1,758, a margin of 31 points, down from Trump's 44-point win in 2024. Hobbs won statewide by 13 points, and Arizona as a whole shifted 19 points left.

The county's shift was smaller than most in the state. It ranks 12th of 15 Arizona counties by move, where the typical county shifted 18 points. Gila moved about as much (13 points), while Graham moved 18 and Greenlee 30. Only 5,272 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

04001.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Hobbs beat Biggs in Apache County by 18,109 votes to 7,820, a Democratic margin of 39 points. In 2024 Harris carried the county by 19, so it moved 20 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than the state's 19-point swing, the typical Arizona county's 18 and the typical national county's 14. Apache ranks fifth of Arizona's 15 counties by move, all of which shifted left. Among similar counties, Santa Cruz moved 27 points, Coconino 18 and Pima 16.

About 26,730 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

04015.t:
In the governor's race, Biggs carried Mohave County over Hobbs by 44 points, 55,381 votes to 21,128. That is still a wide Republican win, but narrower than Trump's 56-point margin here in 2024, a 12-point move toward the Democrats. Every Arizona county moved left, and Mohave moved the least of all 15. The typical county shifted 18 points and the state 19. Comparable counties moved more: Graham 18 points, La Paz 13 and Gila 13.

Turnout was 78,104 votes, 71% of the 110,450 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04009.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Biggs carried Graham County over Hobbs by 6,651 votes to 3,504, a Republican margin of 30 points. That is 18 points closer than Trump's 48-point win over Harris here in 2024, and it matches the typical move among Arizona's 15 counties, all of which shifted toward the Democrats. Statewide the swing was 19 points, and Hobbs won by 13.

Turnout fell sharply: 10,383 votes were cast, about 68% of the 15,183 cast in 2024. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Graham moved more than La Paz and Gila, both 13 points, but well short of Greenlee's 30.

04023.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Santa Cruz County gave Hobbs 9,783 votes to Biggs's 3,593, a Democratic margin of 45 points. In 2024 Harris carried it by 19, so the county moved 27 points toward the Democrats, the third-largest shift among Arizona's 15 counties. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 18 points, and the state as a whole by 19.

The swing also outpaced comparable Democratic-leaning counties: Apache moved 20 points, Coconino 18 and Pima 16. But turnout fell sharply, to 13,695 votes, or 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04017.t:
In the race for governor between Hobbs and Biggs, Navajo County stayed Republican but by much less than in 2024. Biggs carried it 19,578 to 18,945, a margin of 2 points, after Trump won it by 17. That 16-point shift toward the Democrats is a little smaller than the typical Arizona county's 18-point move and the state's 19-point swing; all 15 counties moved left. Among similar counties, Cochise moved about as much (16 points), Pinal somewhat more (19), and Yuma far more (27), flipping to the Democrats.

Turnout was 39,575 votes, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

04021.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Pinal County stayed Republican but by a much smaller margin. Biggs led Hobbs 80,133 to 75,541, about 3 points, after Trump carried the county by 22 in 2024. That 19-point move toward the Democrats is slightly larger than the typical Arizona county's 18 and ranks sixth of the state's 15, all of which moved left. Hobbs won statewide by 13.

Comparable counties moved by different amounts. Cochise and Navajo shifted about 16 points, while Yuma swung 27 and flipped to Hobbs. Pinal cast 158,896 votes, about 76% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04019.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Pima County gave Hobbs 261,121 votes to Biggs's 135,336, a Democratic margin of 31 points. Harris carried it by 15 points in 2024, so the county moved 16 points toward the Democrats. That is a little less than the statewide shift of 19 and the typical Arizona county's 18. All 15 counties in the state moved left. Pima ranks 10th by size of move and second by votes cast. Counties with similar 2024 results moved further: Coconino by 18 points, Apache by 20 and Santa Cruz by 27.

Turnout was 404,819, or 79% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04027.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Yuma County swung from a 20-point win for Trump in 2024 to a 7-point lead for Hobbs over Biggs, 17,588 votes to 15,320. That 27-point move toward the Democrats is the second-largest of Arizona's 15 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Arizona county moved 18 points, and the state as a whole moved 19. Similar counties moved less: Navajo 16, Cochise 16 and Pinal 19, and all three still favored Biggs.

Only 69% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 33,791 ballots counted so far are half of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

04011.t:
In the governor's race between Hobbs and Biggs, Greenlee County moved further toward the Democrats than any other county in Arizona. Trump carried it by 41 points in 2024; Biggs carried it by 11, winning 1,116 votes to Hobbs's 884. That 30-point move was well beyond the statewide shift of 19 points and the typical Arizona county's 18. It was also larger than in comparable Republican-leaning counties: La Paz moved 13 points, Gila 13 and Graham 18.

Only 2,066 votes were cast, 62% of the 2024 total and the fewest of any county in the state. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04003.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Cochise County backed Biggs over Hobbs by about 7 points, 24,091 votes to 20,916. Trump had carried it by 23 points in 2024, so the county moved 16 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly less than the typical Arizona county (18 points), where all 15 moved left, and more than the typical county nationally (14 points). Among similar Arizona counties, Navajo moved about the same (16 points), Pinal a little more (19), and Yuma far more (27), flipping to Hobbs.

About 46,121 votes were cast, 78% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

04025.t:
In the race for Arizona governor, Yavapai County stayed firmly Republican but moved 12 points toward the Democrats. Biggs carried it 72,101 to 45,898 over Hobbs, a margin of 22 points, down from Trump's 34-point win over Harris in 2024. Hobbs won statewide by 13 points.

All 15 Arizona counties moved left, and Yavapai's shift was the second smallest, below the state's typical move of 18 points and the national typical move of 14. Similar Gila County moved 13 points, while Pinal and Cochise moved 19 and 16. About 120,000 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.
